lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Daniel? Is that you?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Maya! Wow, long time no see.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I know. It's been ages. How have you been?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Pretty good, actually. I moved back to the neighborhood last month.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Really? I thought you were still living in Seattle.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I was, but I left my old job two years ago. I work from home now, so I can live pretty much anywhere.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That's a big change. Do you like being back?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So far, yes. The area is really different now, though. This coffee shop used to be a bookstore.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That's right. I used to spend hours there on weekends.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Are you still working at the hospital?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes, but I don't work on the wards anymore. I moved into staff training last year.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That makes sense. You were always good at explaining things.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Thanks. What about your photography? Do you still take pictures?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Not as much as I used to, but I still take some on weekends.

lines.speaker: Barista
lines.text: Large coffee for Daniel!

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That's me. Listen, I have to get going, but we should really catch up.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Definitely. Are you free sometime next week?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I think so. Let me check my schedule and get back to you.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Sounds good. It was really nice seeing you.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: You too. And this time, let's not wait another eight years.
